sources_considered.why: Independent Tow Center test of Grok-3 (beta) search in February 2025. It covers a news-citation task, not DeepSearch reports, so I use it as context.
It evaluates Perplexity's Deep Research using Grok 3 as the topic, not Grok 3 DeepSearch itself.

evidence_items.publisher: Columbia Journalism Review / Tow Center for Digital Journalism
evidence_items.locator: section 'Chatbots’ responses to our queries were often confidently wrong', paragraph 1

receipt.public_excerpt: Across different platforms, the level of inaccuracy varied, with Perplexity answering 37 percent of the queries incorrectly, while Grok 3 had a much higher error rate, answering 94 percent of the queries incorrectly.

evidence_items.explanation: Independent testing of Grok-3 (beta) search found very frequent errors. But the task was identifying news articles, not DeepSearch reports, and it does not measure how subtle the errors were.

evidence_items.publisher: Columbia Journalism Review / Tow Center for Digital Journalism
evidence_items.locator: section 'Premium models provided more confidently incorrect answers than their free counterparts', paragraph 2

receipt.public_excerpt: their authoritative conversational tone, which can make it difficult for users to distinguish between accurate and inaccurate information.

evidence_items.explanation: The researchers judged that confident tone in these tools, Grok 3 included, makes errors hard to tell apart from accurate answers. This relates to the 'difficult to detect' part, but not for DeepSearch reports specifically.

unresolved_gaps: I found no independent, systematic evaluation of Grok 3 DeepSearch reports specifically from around launch.
The Tow Center test covers Grok-3 search on a citation task. Many of its errors, such as broken URLs, are easy to spot, so it does not show 'subtle' errors in reports.
